claims.text: **Theorem.** Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) be bigrassmannian, with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put \[ q=n-r,\quad i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j), \] \[ A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad Q=J_v/A_+J_v. \] Then both \[ G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\} \quad\text{and}\quad G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\} \] map to homogeneous integral bases of \(Q\). Hence both families minimally generate \(J_v\). In particular, \[ Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z\,e_\rho,\qquad \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|, \] \[ H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z, \] and \(Q_d\) is torsion-free. The basis \(e_\rho\) admits the perfect integral degree-complement pairing \[ \langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee},\qquad \rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1), \] between \(Q_d\) and \(Q_{2ij+ab-d}\). The lower-family generation and its no-syzygy mechanism are grounded in the supplied full text. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
A parameter-uniform closed formula for the unimodular change-of-basis matrix from the ordered \(G_L\)-basis to the ordered \(G_R\)-basis is not established.
